extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers (PAOs), commanders, and personnel responsible for media relations and release of information
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Army public affairs and media relations covering travel, accreditation, release authorities, OPSEC/privacy constraints, crisis communications, and permissible media coverage. Intended to govern how PA personnel and commanders facilitate, approve, and coordinate information and media access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonlocal media travel requires DoD approval
rubrics_metrics.description: All nonlocal media travel requires DoD approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA personnel should review DoD instructions, operation orders, and approved PA guidance as there may be preexisting DoD instructions granting approval to travel that (1) is primarily in the interest of the DoD; (2) exists when commercial transportation is not available or is otherwise inadequate to fulfill mission objectives, or an individual is in immediate danger of loss of life, limb, or sight; or (3) is available on a space available, noninterference basis on previously scheduled flights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions permitting nonlocal media travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonlocal media travel may be approved under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval may be granted when: (1) travel by military transportation is an integral part of the story (evacuations, maneuvers, troop movement) and limited to the assignment; (2) proposed coverage is of a major emergency nature and coverage would be seriously impaired or delayed without military transportation (requests under this paragraph submitted directly to OCPA Media Relations Division by fastest means); (3) travel is of special interest to the Army/command and is part of an approved PA project. Transportation must not be used solely for point-to-point movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonlocal travel request procedures and required information
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for forwarding and content of nonlocal media travel requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward requests through command channels to OCPA Media Relations Division. Ensure requests contain dates of travel, destinations, justification, and a point of contact who will: (a) be familiar with regulations and directives on such travel for all services; (b) ensure media are briefed on purpose and appropriate security matters; (c) brief media on passport, visa, immunization, and other requirements; (d) ensure media have proper protective gear if required; (e) submit a news roll-up including clippings or summaries of radio/TV coverage resulting from the travel through channels to OCPA following the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAOs are not required to accompany media
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs are not required to accompany media representatives on nonlocal travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special travel categories and authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities for approving certain categories of PA travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State adjutants general approve PA travel within their respective states. NGB PA office approves local travel to facilities outside their states or territories. Other media travel involving ARNG units requires DoD approval. Air transportation procedures for Members of Congress and their staffs are in AR 1–20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Army aircraft for PA or related travel — permitted examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of PA activities that may qualify for travel in Army-owned or -controlled aircraft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include invitational and other authorized travel to support approved PA activities (tours/conferences sponsored by DA and DoD); tours and PA activities arranged jointly with another federal agency or foreign government; authors and writers covering approved Army programs when travel is integral to the story (space-available); guests of SECDEF or SECARMY participating in official programs (e.g., JCOC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Army aircraft — prohibited or restricted flights
rubrics_metrics.description: Flights for which approval may not be provided under this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval may not be provided for: (1) an aircraft flight during which a record attempt is made; (2) a first flight on an aircraft just entering the inventory; (3) a first flight over an isolated geographical area; (4) any other flight of similar or special nature where abnormal conditions may exist. Army aviation assets are not used to transport persons costumed as holiday characters (Santa, Easter bunnies, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation flight policy for community engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Orientation flights to support community engagement are allowed with conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to improve understanding of the Army mission. Flights may be provided only in suitable passenger-carrying aircraft. Travelers must wear proper organizational uniforms if applicable and present proper identification. Written parental consent required for passengers 18 years or under. Orientation flights will normally originate and terminate at the point of origin or nearby; commanders of ACOMs, ASCCs, and DRUs may grant exceptions case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitating media visits — general principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitation of news media representatives is a PA function and part of the command PA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA staff should build and maintain positive professional relationships with news media representatives; reporters manage key channels that PA must leverage. Senior commanders will cooperate in a timely manner with bona fide media who request permission to visit an installation. OCPA may assume release authority for controversial topics or subjects of national interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media access restrictions and OPSEC/privacy/security limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Media are restricted from areas requiring controlled access for OPSEC, Privacy Act, criminal justice, or other security concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media may visit exercises, deployments, activities, or areas normally open to the public to cover releasable information. Local procedures will be developed to facilitate media during disaster and civil disturbance conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commander-established ground rules and media compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders will establish ground rules to ensure free flow of information while safeguarding sensitive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media representatives are responsible for adhering to ground rules. Those who violate ground rules risk losing credentials and future access. If sensitive information is accidentally revealed, PA representative should explain sensitivity and request non-publication; if media refuse, report incident to commander who may notify supervisor, cancel credential, or direct escort off installation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command/PA staff commentary on media coverage on unit social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted sharing or comment on media coverage on unit social media channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders and PA staff are permitted to share or comment on media coverage specific to their unit on unit social media channels, but not on the media organization's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: News media accreditation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accreditation validates credentials but does not grant special privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders may supplement accreditation for a specific event but accreditation must not be made cumbersome, overly extensive, or obtrusive to the point of making coverage difficult. Stars and Stripes reporters are treated as civilian news media for credentialing (see DoDD 5122.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official discussions with the media
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel are encouraged to speak candidly with media about unclassified matters within their knowledge and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior commanders and staff officers are expected to discuss military matters within their purview. PAOs will seek out experts to brief media in support of queries or requests for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial discussions (personal capacity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel may agree to media interviews in an unofficial capacity and express personal opinions, with constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel must inform their PA office that the interview occurred or will occur. They should discuss unclassified matters they have personal knowledge about. When questioned on policy, classified matters, or outside their scope, they must state they cannot speak for the Army/DoD and refer media to command PA office. When speaking unofficially, Soldiers will not be in uniform unless appropriately authorized by AR 670–1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographing/recording personnel in hostile areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorize media access to operational locations using common sense and safety/security awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAO will encourage compliance with local release proprieties. If a photographer persists in taking photographs related to their story, the PAO should not attempt to recover the recording medium, but will immediately report the problem through PA channels to higher headquarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media coverage of equipment testing and evaluation prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Media coverage of developmental, technological validation, or operational testing and evaluation of Army systems is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media coverage of battle labs and warfighting experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: All media coverage of Army battle labs and Army warfighting experiments requires OCPA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of official information requires security and PA clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any official information intended for public release that pertains to military matters, national security, or subjects of significant concern to DoD must be cleared by appropriate security review and PA offices prior to release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes materials placed on the internet or released via similar electronic media. All Soldiers, DA Civilians, and contractors who publish, administer, or moderate information or documents on the public domain for official purposes will complete Army OPSEC Training for External Official Presences online training (per DoDI 5230.29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial and objective dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about the United States and its allies will be disseminated impartially and objectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communication responsibilities and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Commander responsible for crisis communication; PAO is the commander's agent for planning and execution; timeliness is critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commander is ultimately responsible; PAO must assist and create crisis communication plans. Mitigate withholding information and release what is known as soon as possible. PA and SJA must determine legality of releasing information during crisis. If crisis involves a felony crime, after immediate public safety concerns are addressed, coordinate investigative-type releases with USACIC and OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal privacy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases must comply with the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 USC 552a) as implemented by AR 25–22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Privacy Act generally prohibits publicly releasing certain items of information about an individual without consent. All Army personnel and releases will comply with these prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health information security compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases must comply with PL 104–191 and related DoD/DoD directives regarding protected health information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Law 104–191, implemented by DoDM 6025.18 and DoDI 8580.02, generally prohibits publicly releasing certain items of information about an individual without consent. All Army personnel and releases will comply with these prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information categories requiring OSD/OCPA clearance prior to release
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories of information must be coordinated and submitted to OCPA Media Relations Division for OSD clearance prior to release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information that meets any of the criteria below requires OSD clearance prior to release: (1) originates from or is proposed for release at the seat of government; (2) is or could become an item of national or international interest; (3) has foreign policy or foreign relations implications; (4) concerns high-level military or DoD policy; (5) concerns U.S. Government policy or policy of other agencies; (6) concerns casualties for release by OSD; (7) concerns subjects of potential controversy among services or other federal agencies; (8) initial information on new weapons, weapon systems, significant modifications, or improvements; (9) information on significant military operations, potential operations, and military exercises; (10) information on military applications and operations in space; (11) information on WMD and related research/defense testing/production/policies (including subitems: nuclear effects research; chemical warfare and defensive biological/toxic research; high-energy lasers and particle beams technology; CBRNE defense testing and production, policies, programs, activities); (12) information on National Command Authorities and their command posts; (13) information and materials involving critical military technology; (14) information concerning communications security, electronic warfare, signal intelligence, and computer security; (15) initial announcement of general officer assignments; (16) initial announcement of awarded Army contracts per FAR/DFARS/AFARS; (17) lists of names or duty addresses of military personnel assigned to units that are sensitive, routinely deployed, or stationed in a foreign territory; (18) casualty information on key U.S. Government personnel or equivalent foreign government personnel; (19) information on activation, inactivation, or reorganization of Army brigade or larger units; (20) information on DoD counterterrorist activities as defined by DoD policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: HQDA (OCPA) release and coordination authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: OCPA has authority to release information about the Army as a whole and coordinates on congressional inquiries and Pentagon events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCPA normally obtains information from ARSTAF agencies and clears with OSD and the Secretariat as necessary. OCPA will coordinate with OCLL, other DA staff agencies, and ATSD (PA) on replies to congressional inquiries with PA implications prior to forwarding to Congress. Interviews and press conferences at the Pentagon will be coordinated with OCPA and monitored by PAO or PA liaison officer of the ARSTAF agency concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release authorities and coordination for commands below HQDA
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders below HQDA authorized to release information wholly within their mission and scope provided it is not restricted by higher-level provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information is normally submitted to the PAO for preparation and security review. PAO will obtain clearance from the commander or forward to appropriate headquarters. Commanders below HQDA will inform OCPA directly while coordinating through command channels when national news media requests are received. In deployed environments, adhere to guidance from higher headquarters (combatant commanders, NATO). If a crisis/emerging event occurs, first PAO on scene will coordinate with next higher headquarters to define PA responsibilities and release authority. When supporting other federal agencies, use operational chain of command and PA channels of supported agencies to coordinate visits, media opportunities, and information release. Releasing military intelligence or intelligence-related information must be authorized by INSCOM or appropriate intelligence authorities. Releasing operational information on ARSOFs coordinated with USASOC. Releasing felony-related criminal investigative information must be coordinated with and authorized by USACIC. Coordinate with PAO responsible for area when releasing training/movement info for units deploying elsewhere. OCONUS PAOs may be NATO/allied or other host nation PAOs depending on operation. Coordinate with State Department before releasing information about U.S. forces supporting another nation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding information and OPSEC review
rubrics_metrics.description: Safeguarded information must not be discussed, shown, or made available to unauthorized individuals and must be reviewed for OPSEC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Army personnel must support the Army's OPSEC program. Information, materials, or records must be reviewed for OPSEC considerations in accordance with AR 530–1 prior to public release. The staff office or agency providing information to PA should accomplish OPSEC reviews. Releasable information must be accurate and adhere to published DoD and Army policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of Army records
rubrics_metrics.description: Army records will be released only when approved by appropriate authority and in accordance with AR 25–22 and AR 25–55.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials who release records will inform their PAO if records contain controversial information; PAOs will notify commanders and OCPA. If a record would be released if requested under FOIA, then it should be released to media representatives if requested through PA channels (precludes invoking FOIA and provides timely information to the public).

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing in action and whereabouts unknown releases
rubrics_metrics.description: All information released regarding missing in action or duty status whereabouts unknown must follow DoDI 1300.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military accidents — cooperation and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with national security, give maximum cooperation to U.S. news representatives covering military accidents occurring outside military installations, with exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not apply to accidents involving CBRNE weapons/research or military accidents occurring OCONUS, U.S. territories, or possessions — guidance given in treaties and laws of other nations in coordination with combatant commands. Civilian law enforcement and emergency response agencies may be on scene before the military. Commanders or activities will coordinate and plan with agencies before an incident and advise them they may be called upon for assistance when military accidents occur in their areas and advise of relevant USC sections (18 USC 793(d),(e), 18 USC 795, 18 USC 797) that make photographing, publishing, or refusing to surrender classified information unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of accidents involving military personnel or equipment — casualty information rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Public release of information on injured or deceased personnel will be made as soon as possible, within Privacy Act constraints, after coordination with OCPA/HQDA and confirmation next of kin have been notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-story, single-release coverage preferred. Normally release: (1) announcement that an accident occurred; (2) location/time; (3) names/city/state of injured withheld until consent/next of kin notified; (4) names/city/state of deceased withheld until 24 hours after next of kin notification; (5) before official findings: 'An investigation is being conducted to determine the cause.' (6) To reduce anxiety, names should be released as soon as possible. Civilian aircraft under military charter considered military aircraft for release. PAO nearest scene coordinates with local law enforcement, transportation companies, and Army casualty personnel to ensure next of kin notified prior to public release. Additional personal info about deceased/injured must be approved by Servicemember or next of kin. Casualty info on key U.S. Government personnel released only at specified authorities (White House Press Secretary, ATSD (PA), or commander concerned depending on rank/position). Follow-up info may be released by local PAOs with immediate OCPA notification. OCONUS accidents require embassy/consulate coordination; names of special operations personnel coordinated with USASOC prior to release. Information from official investigations regarding line-of-duty status or findings of misconduct will not be released without approval of Adjutant General/HQDA as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel under treatment in Army medical facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about patients in Army medical facilities released only in accordance with FOIA, Privacy Act, and PL 104–191.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographical data other than that releasable under AR 25–22, protected health information, and descriptions of specific condition will not be released without prior consent recorded on DA Form 4876. Authority to release information on personnel from other services or agencies rests with that service/agency; Army PAOs assume responsibility only upon official request. Permission to photograph/record a patient given only with prior informed written consent and attending physician/medical facility commander determination that activity will not jeopardize patient welfare; photographing prohibited when it infringes on privacy or causes embarrassment. Releasing info or permitting interviews with psychiatric or other mental health patients is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel in alcohol and drug abuse control programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Public release of information regarding personnel participating in alcohol and drug abuse control programs is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: USACIC personnel or activities release coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Public release about USACIC personnel, activities, regulations, or investigations must be coordinated in advance with OCPA and USACIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of criminal investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, no information should be released concerning ongoing investigations without close coordination with appropriate law enforcement agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAO may acknowledge existence of an investigation after coordination, but released information cannot violate the Privacy Act or impede an ongoing criminal investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of courts-martial — media recording and attendance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge is final approval authority on media attendance, photographing, video, social media, or other recording at courts-martial; guidance provided unless more restrictive measures needed for fair trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographing or video recording courtroom interior may be permitted when persons involved are not present. During trial, photographing/video of the accused may be permitted outdoors in public view. Photographing/video of the accused in courtroom, cell, cellblock, prison yard, or similar area or in presence of other prisoners is not permitted. PAO will coordinate to accommodate coverage including courtroom pool reporting and a separate media center near the courtroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation and debarment cases — coordination and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain close liaison with Office of the General Counsel or SJA to avoid premature release of information about litigation or debarment cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters in litigation or with potential for litigation will not be discussed unless information is public record. PAO and SJA will coordinate responses. For debarments, PA offices will not release debarment information prior to consultation with SJA and judge advocate confirmation of final decision; may acknowledge that a company has been proposed for debarment but will refer media to the contractor regarding basis/status without comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspector General records — release authority
rubrics_metrics.description: IG records are privileged documents; unauthorized use or release can compromise IG effectiveness and confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IG is the designated release authority for all IG records (see AR 20–1). IG records are property of SECARMY and include USAR IG and ARNGUS IG records concerning federal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of information on units — deployments and force structure changes
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD provides initial public release for deployments of units brigade combat team level and above; HQDA coordinates initial release for certain activations/inactivations/reorganizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders will notify Families and coordinate congressional notification through OCLL prior to initial announcement. Separate smaller units not announced by DoD/OCPA may make public announcement following deployment orders and Family notification. For activations/inactivations/reorganizations, initial release of Regular Army units of brigade or larger will be made at HQDA through OSD. Smaller Regular Army units may be announced by ASCC, ACOM, or DRU except when criteria in paragraph 7–6 apply — in such cases HQDA/OSD issues initial release. Initial public release will not be made until authorized by DCS, G–3/5/7 and following release to Members of Congress as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of unit information — safeguarded details and RC/OCONUS coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain unit information is generally not releasable; coordinate releases for RC units and when involving other nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguarded information generally not releasable includes exact personnel strength/composition, status/amounts/quality of equipment, combat efficiency, deployment of units to combat areas. For RC units: USAR information released by ARHQ–FB about local units; CNGB ensures National Guard Bureau notifies unit and state adjutant general may release local info once notified. When activation/restationing involves another nation, HQDA coordination with ASCC, COCOM, U.S. Embassy PA teams and host nation authority is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation activation/inactivation/realignment release criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate and timely information consistent with security will be released when decisions have been made to activate/inactivate/realign installations/facilities and associated personnel reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial announcements for such actions are made at HQDA through OSD when action requires prior notification of Congress (e.g., personnel reductions in near-term or over 18-36 months, reductions due to commercial activity, accessing Government installations/facilities, generated congressional/public interest, or public controversy during decision-making). Criteria flexible and OCPA may make exceptions; OCPA will issue guidance prior to scheduled announcements. Army personnel should avoid statements interpreted as official that invite speculation about inactivations/realignments/reductions. Commanders will provide mechanism for public feedback on realignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and movement of units — release rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on unit training or movement not safeguarded may be released by responsible commander except for major or joint exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial release of information on major Army exercises will be made at HQDA through OSD. Major joint exercises initial release by OSD with later announcements by joint commander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographing military installations or equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Public access and photographing rules for installations and equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access to Army installations determined by local commands. Photographing historical buildings or areas of public interest for private use generally permitted but subject to local command approval. Ground/aerial photographs, sketches, or graphic representations of classified military equipment or installations designated as restricted areas are punishable by law (18 USC 795). Reproducing, publishing, or selling such material is punishable unless it indicates it has been reviewed and cleared for release by proper authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release about foreign military personnel attending U.S. Army schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate interview requests concerning foreign military personnel attending U.S. Army schools with the proper country's senior officer in residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of Army studies — prohibition on premature release
rubrics_metrics.description: Premature release of emerging results of Army studies and analyses before official approval is prohibited.
